claims.quote: We require of each that he shall make the same effort; that is, we demand of him the best service it is in his power to give.
claims.description: All citizens receive equal shares regardless of output; each gives their best effort.

claims.quote: there is no idea in the modern social economy which at all corresponds with what was meant by wages in your day.
claims.description: Wages abolished in favor of equal credit.

claims.quote: The fact that the nation is the sole capitalist and land-owner of course restricts the individual's possessions to his annual credit, and what personal and household belongings he may have procured with it.
claims.description: The nation owns all capital and land; individuals hold annual credits.

claims.quote: We require, indeed, by law that every man shall serve the nation for a fixed period, instead of leaving him his choice, as you did, between working, stealing, or starving.
claims.description: Universal compulsory industrial service for a fixed period.

claims.quote: So you see that though we have abolished poverty and the fear of it, and inordinate luxury with the hope of it
With us, diligence in the national service is the sole and certain way to public repute, social distinction, and official power.
claims.description: Social rank and honor determined by service to the nation rather than money.

claims.quote: The assortment in all is exactly the same, representing as it does in each case samples of all the varieties produced or imported by the United States.
claims.description: Sample stores with identical national assortments replace competing retail shops.

claims.quote: These printed cards, for which the government authorities are responsible, give us all the information we can possibly need.
claims.description: Government-certified product information cards replace salesmanship.

claims.quote: after the clerk had punched the value of her purchase out of the credit card she gave him
claims.description: Purchases are paid by punching value off a credit card issued by the state.

claims.quote: The packages are then delivered by larger tubes to the city districts, and thence distributed to the houses.
claims.description: Pneumatic tube delivery of purchased goods to homes.

claims.quote: The goods, with these exceptions, are all at the great central warehouse of the city, to which they are shipped directly from the producers.
claims.description: Direct producer-to-warehouse distribution eliminates wholesalers and retailers.

claims.quote: These halls are connected by telephone with all the houses of the city whose people care to pay the small fee, and there are none, you may be sure, who do not.
claims.description: Music piped by telephone line from concert halls to homes on demand, around the clock.

claims.quote: All our bedchambers have a telephone attachment at the head of the bed by which any person who may be sleepless can command music at pleasure, of the sort suited to the mood.
claims.description: Bedside telephone receivers deliver music on demand.

claims.quote: All the really fine singers and players are in the musical service, and the rest of us hold our peace for the main part.
claims.description: Professional musicians are a public service; amateurs rarely perform.

claims.quote: The rents which the nation receives for these houses vary, according to size, elegance, and location, so that everybody can find something to suit.
claims.description: The state owns housing and charges rent against equal incomes.

claims.quote: His credit, like an annuity in your day, ceases on his death, with the allowance of a fixed sum for funeral expenses.
claims.description: An individual's state credit ends at death; no accumulation of wealth.
